quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What is a benefit of wearing gloves while riding?

options.text: They make the motorcycle easier to control.
They help other drivers see you.
They give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: They give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best traction?
questions.explanation: Many surfaces create poor traction. Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted road markings, and metal covers are all more dangerous for motorcycles than dry pavement.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Speed limit and other regulatory signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What best protects against head and neck injuries in a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the most important thing you can do to reduce head and neck injuries in a crash.

questions.question: What is a danger of riding next to parked cars?

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A car may pull out suddenly into your path.
Drivers may go slowly looking for a spot.
The road surface may be uneven.

questions.correctAnswerText: A car may pull out suddenly into your path.
questions.explanation: Parked cars create several dangers. A driver may pull out without looking. Car doors may open into your lane. Pedestrians may step out from between cars.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: Where can you find the best information about your specific motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Read your motorcycle's owner's manual before you ride it for the first time. This is especially important if you are borrowing someone else's motorcycle.

questions.question: When should you wear riding gloves?

options.text: Never, because they make your hands too hot
Always, to get a better grip on the handlebars
Never, because they make controls harder to use

questions.correctAnswerText: Always, to get a better grip on the handlebars
questions.explanation: Wear leather or durable gloves when riding. They improve your grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What is true about an approved helmet?

options.text: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see far enough to the sides for safe riding
questions.explanation: A U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet will not limit your vision. It lets you see as far to the sides as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: Which of these does not need regular checking?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small mechanical problems on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: Your body can only remove alcohol through:
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Which one is NOT a slippery surface?

options.text: A strip of oil in the center of a lane

questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, oil, and metal road covers are all slippery. Dry pavement is not slippery.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:
questions.explanation: A good helmet is the best protection against head and neck injuries if you have an accident.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: For the best protection, boots or shoes should:

options.text: Be made of a soft material.
Have long laces that are not tucked in.
Cover the ankle and provide support.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the ankle and provide support.
questions.explanation: Choose tall, sturdy boots or shoes that cover and support your ankles. Keep heels low so they don't catch on surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Space between your motorcycle and other vehicles allows you to:

options.text: Have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
Stay in one area of the lane with limited movement.
Rely on others to identify hazards.
Go faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle gives you time and space to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicle lights.
More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because visibility is reduced. You cannot see and be seen as easily as during the day. Shadows and light are different, making it harder to judge distances.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders can improve visibility by:
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors with reflective material. Use your headlight at all times. Use your signals and brake light properly. These steps help other drivers see you.

questions.question: Keep an adequate following distance behind other vehicles to:

options.text: Give yourself time and space to identify and react to hazards.
Help traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself time and space to identify and react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Adequate following distance gives you space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also gives you a better view of road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: When passing parked vehicles, riders should be careful of:

options.text: Motorists looking for a place to park.

questions.explanation: When passing parked vehicles, be careful. Cars may suddenly pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of which material for the best protection?
questions.explanation: Leather or other durable materials provide the best protection for riding gloves.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle can cause serious crashes. Check your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. How can you be more visible?
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright-colored clothing while riding to stay visible, even during the day.

questions.question: What should you do with your feet when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Keep them firmly on the footrests
Keep them away from the controls

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep them firmly on the footrests
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not drag them or point your toes down. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: When should a rider use their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down, stopping, at intersections, changing lanes, and turning.
